title: Three Sum
statement_md:
Given an integer array `nums`, find every **distinct** triplet of values `[a, b, c]`, taken from three different positions, with `a + b + c == 0`.

Two triplets are the same if they contain the same values, no matter the order or which positions they came from — report each distinct triplet once. Return the triplets in any order; the values inside a triplet may be in any order too.

examples.explanation: Both triplets sum to zero; the two 1s come from different positions.
Many choices of positions all give the same triplet, which is reported once.
No three values sum to zero.

tests.explain_on_fail: Two distinct triplets, one of which uses a repeated value.
Duplicate triplets must be reported only once.
Several triplets share values — each distinct triplet appears once.
A repeated value is needed to form the only triplet.
Heavy duplication — skip repeated values so no triplet is reported twice.
Values at the edges of the allowed range.
A large input with many repeated values — sort, then use two pointers (O(n²)), not three nested loops.
A large input of distinct values with only a few solutions.

editorial_md:
### Intuition
Sorting turns the problem into many "two sum on a sorted array" problems. Fix the first value `nums[i]`; the other two must sum to `-nums[i]`, which two pointers find in one sweep of the rest of the array. Sorting also makes duplicates adjacent, so they are easy to skip.

### Algorithm
1. Sort `nums`.
2. For each `i` (skipping a value equal to the previous one), set `lo = i + 1`, `hi = n − 1`.
3. Move `lo` right when the sum is too small, `hi` left when it is too large. On a hit, record the triplet and move `lo` past any copies of the same value.
4. Once `nums[i] > 0` no more triplets are possible.

```python
def threeSum(nums):
    nums = sorted(nums)
    n = len(nums)
    out = []
    for i in range(n - 2):
        if nums[i] > 0:
            break
        if i > 0 and nums[i] == nums[i - 1]:
            continue
        lo, hi = i + 1, n - 1
        while lo < hi:
            total = nums[i] + nums[lo] + nums[hi]
            if total < 0:
                lo += 1
            elif total > 0:
                hi -= 1
            else:
                out.append([nums[i], nums[lo], nums[hi]])
                lo += 1
                hi -= 1
                while lo < hi and nums[lo] == nums[lo - 1]:
                    lo += 1
    return out
```

### Complexity
O(n²) time, O(1) extra space apart from the sort and the output. Three nested loops are O(n³) and far too slow at n = 3000.

hints.body_md: If you fix one value of the triplet, what are you looking for among the remaining values?
Sort first. Fix `nums[i]`; the other two values must sum to `-nums[i]`, and on a sorted suffix two pointers find all such pairs in one pass. Skip equal neighbours to avoid duplicate triplets.

```
sort nums
for i in 0..n-3:
    if i > 0 and nums[i] == nums[i-1]: continue
    lo = i + 1, hi = n - 1
    while lo < hi:
        sum = nums[i] + nums[lo] + nums[hi]
        if sum < 0: lo++  elif sum > 0: hi--
        else: record; lo++; hi--; skip duplicate nums[lo]
```
Deduplicate the first value with `if i > 0 and nums[i] == nums[i - 1]: continue`, and after a hit advance past repeats with `while lo < hi and nums[lo] == nums[lo - 1]: lo += 1`.
